note: Public GCI changelog. Mirrors the Methodology changelog table in docs/kb/03-scoring.md. Every entry that moves a published number has matching rows in score_ledger.jsonl.

entries.change: Infosys FY24 operating margin is now on the record: guided 20%–22% in the 13 April 2023 results release, actual 20.7% in the 18 April 2024 results release, inside the band. The row is one closed period, so it stays beside the score and the composite stays 76.5. A second metric moves the confidence tier from provisional to deep, so Infosys can appear on the Public Snapshot.

Each scored row can now record the reporting basis, unit, and scope of the guidance and of the actual. When both sides are filled and they differ, that row stays outside the score. A blank side is treated as unknown and still scores, so no published level moves. Infosys FY24 constant-currency revenue remains a miss: guided 4–7%, actual 1.4% in constant currency, and the January revision was 1.5–2%. Reported rupee revenue growth of 4.7% is a different basis and cannot close the constant-currency row.

Ledger correction, no score changed on the site. When the v4.2 release was deployed, the score ledger recorded Axis Bank, Adani Ports, Apollo Hospitals and HDFC Life as withdrawn. Their scores had been read while the service was still loading their filing citations. The published levels were never withdrawn. Correcting rows restore Axis Bank 90.7 (the v4.2 level), Adani Ports 58.7, Apollo Hospitals 60.4 and HDFC Life 87.8. The earlier rows stay in the ledger, which is append-only.

Two changes to how a result is compared with its guided range (v4.2). First, each metric now has a direction. For most metrics a result above the range is a beat. For working-capital days the beat is below the range. For capex and R&D spend, landing outside the range either way counts as a miss. Second, every guided range has a minimum half-width before scoring: 2% of the midpoint and, for percentage metrics, never less than 0.1 percentage point. The minimum used to apply only to single-figure guidance and had no absolute floor, so a 3.80% NIM guide was scored against ±0.08 pp. Axis Bank 83.8 → 90.7 (FY25 NIM guided 3.80%, reported 3.98%; still scored as a beat). Infosys 76.5, Cipla 65.5, Adani Ports 58.7, Apollo Hospitals 60.4 and HDFC Life 87.8 are unchanged. Company pages also now say how results have landed against guidance and how guidance moved during the year. That description is not part of the GCI.

Every NSE and BSE listing now carries a coverage status (scored, open period, filing in review, no quantified guidance, or listed only). A published number still requires a guidance quote and a later actual on accepted filings. Machine-extracted rows that pass quote-in-document checks may publish as extracted_verified at the provisional tier and are not ranked. Exchange-filing ingest and extract jobs walk Nifty, then India Top 1000, then the rest of NSE and BSE-only names. A completed lookback with no metric-and-number promise is recorded as no quantified guidance — a coverage finding, not a delivery miss. Infosys 76.5, Cipla 65.5, Axis Bank 83.8, Adani Ports 58.7, Apollo Hospitals 60.4 and HDFC Life 87.8 are unchanged.

Guidance review filed promise citations already stored on the filings, where the guided figure is not the same number as the result. Axis Bank none → 83.8 provisional (FY25 NIM guided 3.80%, actual 3.98%). Adani Ports none → 58.7 provisional (FY25 cargo band 460–480 MMT, actual 450). Apollo Hospitals none → 60.4 provisional (FY24 ARPOB band 6–7%, actual 11%). HDFC Life none → 87.8 provisional (operating RoEV). Rows whose guidance figure is the reported actual stay unscored. Infosys 76.5 and Cipla 65.5 are unchanged.

A row counts when a fetch of both filings contains the recorded quotes. The company page shows the date of that check. A missing quote drops the row; nothing is queued for a person. The 31 March 2027 Sensex and Nifty 50 coverage date is withdrawn. The methodology page states the limitations, including the ±2% band on a single-point guide. In-year revision count, direction, and average move are shown beside the score and are not part of GCI. Infosys 76.5 and Cipla 65.5 are unchanged.

Filing-to-score target published: a reviewed score within 5 business days of the results filing, for filings dated on or after 29 Sep 2026. Methodology and Trust show the observed median from scored rows (today a historical batch reviewed on 29 Sep 2026; live sample is empty). Availability percentages removed from the coverage note until 90 days of measured uptime. Infosys 76.5 and Cipla 65.5 are unchanged.

Every hand-labeled source link is checked for the recorded quote (python -m app.jobs.verify_sources; live refresh at most once per 24 hours). Missing quotes are not citeable and go to the labeling queue. The Trust Center shows how many links verified. Four HTML press pages that do not contain a verifiable quote are excluded until re-cited to a filing: HCLTech FY26 revenue guidance, Maruti FY25 wholesale volume, JSW Steel FY25, Grasim FY25 UltraTech volumes. Infosys 76.5 and Cipla 65.5 are unchanged.

Audit flags (guidance withdrawn, restatement, definition shift) now apply only when an analyst records the flag with their id and a source filing. Keyword matches still surface in the labeling queue as suggestions; they do not move a published score. Dropped guidance stays out of the average and no longer auto-applies the withdrawal deduction. Infosys 76.5 and Cipla 65.5 are unchanged.

A closed result now enters the company score only when both the original guidance and the subsequent actual are cited (source, quote and date). Rows that have the reported actual but not the original guidance filing are labelled pending guidance cite and stay on the company page without contributing points. 37 companies that had been scored from actual-only citations are withdrawn until those promise citations are filled, including Trent (89.9). Infosys stays 76.5 (five dual-cited years of constant-currency revenue guidance); the FY25 operating-margin row is excluded, so the company is provisional (one metric). Cipla 85.2 → 65.5 (only the FY24 EBITDA-margin row remains dual-cited). The Public Snapshot ranks no company until more names reach the Established tier.

Confidence-tier rule clarified: a metric counts toward a company's evidence breadth as soon as it has one closed, analyst-reviewed result, whether it enters the composite or is shown as context. The score formula and every published level are unchanged. Tier moves: Infosys provisional → deep (five closed years of constant-currency revenue guidance plus one closed operating-margin result), Cipla provisional → established (three closed periods across revenue and R&D spend). Hindalco, HDFC Life and Apollo Hospitals gain breadth but remain provisional with fewer than three closed periods. The Public Snapshot now ranks Trent, Cipla and Infosys.

Evidence-weighted composite (v4.1). A metric now enters the company score with weight equal to its number of closed reporting periods (capped at 5); a metric with only one closed period is shown as context and no longer moves the composite when a deeper metric exists. Moved: Infosys 88.2 → 76.5 (FY25 operating-margin row, one period, becomes context; score = five years of constant-currency revenue guidance), Cipla 92.6 → 85.2 (R&D-spend row context), HDFC Life 87.3 → 94.0 (VNB-growth row context), Apollo Hospitals 63.7 → 54.6 (occupancy, EBITDA-margin and revenue rows context). Trent and Hindalco unchanged. Sector shrinkage removed from the method (it was never applied). Every company now carries a confidence tier: provisional (< 3 closed periods or 1 metric), established (≥ 3 periods, ≥ 2 metrics), deep (≥ 5 periods, ≥ 2 metrics). Only established and deep scores are ranked on the Public Snapshot.

Score changes over time (week / month / quarter / year) are shown only when a company has at least four analyst-reviewed reporting dates. Synthetic point-in-time paths that previously filled these chips, the price overlay, lead–lag and correlation panels were removed from public pages; they remain in the Analyst Workbench, labelled experimental.

Infosys 48.2 → 88.2 (logged retrospectively; the move shipped without a changelog entry). In-year revenue-guidance band revisions (July / October / January results releases) are now recorded on the fiscal-year row's revision trail instead of as separate rows, and a placeholder FY24 "dropped restatement sample" row was removed. The guidance-withdrawal (−15), restatement (−15) and definition-shift (−10) deductions that fired on those placeholder rows no longer apply. Definition-shift now compares bands within the same reporting period only; a different band for a different year is not a definition change.

Infosys revenue rows re-cited to SEC-filed results releases (Form 6-K Ex. 99.1): the promise cites the April release that set the band; the actual cites the April release that reported it. FY22 band corrected 10–12% → 12–14% (the IR summary table disagreed with the filing); FY26 as-of date 17 Apr → 23 Apr 2026. FY22 row 60.4 → 61.8 pts; Infosys 48.1 → 48.2. No label changed.

Screener list, Public Snapshot, search and history now apply audit deductions, so every page shows the same number as the company page. Lists had shown the pre-deduction score for 22 audit-flagged names (e.g. Infosys 73.2 list vs 48.2 dossier; Coal India 4.7 vs 0.0).
